title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster, cheaper everyday AI model, across Search, Sheets and the API

kept.claim: Google announced/launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026.
kept.evidence: Google blog dated Nov 12, 2026 ('Today, we're introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen'); Digital Trends published Nov 12, 2026 saying Google 'today launched' it; Notebookcheck: 'Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12'.

kept.claim: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is positioned as Google's fast, efficient 'daily driver' for agentic workflows and everyday tasks, while frontier models Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon handle deep, long-horizon reasoning.
kept.evidence: Google: 'our daily driver for agentic workflows'; Carbon and Argon 'excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning'. Digital Trends paraphrases the same framing.

kept.claim: Hydrogen is the successor to / replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as Google's everyday model.
kept.evidence: Google compares it to teams 'migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash'; Notebookcheck: 'Hydrogen replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as Google's everyday model'.

kept.claim: Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at its high default setting.
kept.evidence: Google: 'finishing tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting'; Digital Trends: 'perform tasks 2.5x faster at its default setting'; Notebookcheck: 'finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than its predecessor'. These are Google's own claims.

kept.claim: Google says Hydrogen cuts fabricated claims by more than 5x versus Gemini 3.8 Flash.
kept.evidence: Google: 'cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x'; Digital Trends: 'more than 5x fewer fabricated claims'; Notebookcheck: 'fabricated claims more than five times less often'.

kept.claim: Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, versus 50 for Gemini 4 Argon.
kept.evidence: Google: 'surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index... (51 vs. 50...)'; Notebookcheck: 'scores 51, one point ahead of the larger Gemini 4 Argon'. Digital Trends says only that it surpasses Argon, with no numbers.

kept.claim: API pricing is flat across the whole 1 million-token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.
kept.evidence: Google: 'priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens'; Notebookcheck: 'Developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across the full context window of 1 million tokens'. Digital Trends gives no price.

kept.claim: Hydrogen has four thinking levels (low, medium, high as the default, and a new xhigh tier).
kept.evidence: Google: 'four thinking levels — low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier'; Digital Trends: 'four thinking levels, with xhigh being the newest addition'; Notebookcheck: 'four thinking levels, including a new xhigh setting'.

kept.claim: Hydrogen is available through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, across all tiers of AI Studio, and in Android Studio.
kept.evidence: Google: 'for all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API'; 'Gemini API in AI Studio and Android Studio'. Digital Trends: 'available through the Gemini API, including in Android Studio, and in Google AI Studio across all tiers'. Notebookcheck: rolling out in 'the Gemini API' (does not mention AI Studio or Android Studio).

kept.claim: Hydrogen is rolling out in Google Search for all users globally, with better understanding of multi-part or typo-ridden queries, more visual responses, and a wider range of links via an upgraded query fan-out technique.
kept.evidence: Google: 'significantly upgrading Search... for all users globally' plus the three improvements. Digital Trends: 'powers Google Search for all users globally' with better understanding, more visual responses and a broader selection of links. Notebookcheck confirms availability in Search for all users worldwide and better handling of multi-part questions and typos, but not the visual or links points.

kept.claim: Hydrogen is rolling out in the Gemini app model drop-down; free users get it only via auto model selection when it is the appropriate model for the prompt.
kept.evidence: Google footnote: 'free users will get access to Gemini 4 Hydrogen via auto model selection when it's the appropriate model for the prompt'; Digital Trends: free users 'get it automatically when the app decides it's the right fit'; Notebookcheck: 'Free users cannot pick Hydrogen themselves'.

kept.claim: Hydrogen is coming to Gemini in Google Sheets, starting with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers (and for eligible business subscriptions per Google).
kept.evidence: Google: 'Gemini in Google Sheets starting with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers' and 'for eligible business subscriptions'. Digital Trends: 'coming to Gemini in Google Sheets, starting with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers'. Notebookcheck does not mention Sheets.

kept.claim: Hydrogen is available in Google Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.
kept.evidence: Google: 'paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity'; Digital Trends: 'in Google Antigravity for users who pay for a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription'.

kept.claim: Enterprises can deploy Hydrogen through Gemini for business / Gemini Enterprise via the API or the model drop-down.
kept.evidence: Google: 'Deploy it in Gemini for business via the API or model drop down'; Digital Trends: 'Enterprises can deploy it via the API or pick it from the model drop-down in Gemini Enterprise'.

kept.claim: Google says Hydrogen reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81% and is up to 2x less likely to bypass permission boundaries when a task is blocked.
kept.evidence: Google: 'reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81%... up to 2x less likely to bypass permission boundaries'; Digital Trends repeats both figures.

kept.claim: In partner tests on complex graphs, SQL and data-heavy enterprise workflows, Hydrogen ran 2x to 2.8x faster than 3.8 Flash while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%.
kept.evidence: Google: 'run 2x to 2.8x faster while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%'. Digital Trends: 'up to 2.8x faster, while using up to 23% fewer tokens' (gives a narrower range than Google).

kept.claim: The 'cheaper' framing is supported only by the published API price and Google's efficiency claims. Neither the Google blog nor Digital Trends states that Hydrogen's price is lower than Gemini 3.8 Flash's. Digital Trends' subhead says 'faster, cheaper' but gives no price.
kept.evidence: Google blog gives the price ($1.50 / $7.50 per million tokens) with no comparison to 3.8 Flash pricing; Digital Trends subhead: 'faster, cheaper' with no price figures in the body.

kept.claim: The Hydrogen announcement is new (Nov 12, 2026) and not older than the sources imply. Digital Trends says it came 'weeks after' Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon.
kept.evidence: Google post dated Nov 12, 2026, last updated Nov 13, 2026; Digital Trends: 'Merely weeks after introducing the Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon'.

dropped.claim: Hydrogen reaches 54 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its highest xhigh thinking setting.
dropped.evidence: Google: 'reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting'. Only the Google blog states this.

dropped.claim: In Gemini in Google Sheets, Hydrogen generates outputs over 30% faster than previous models in Sheets canvas.
dropped.evidence: Google: 'generating outputs over 30% faster than previous models in Sheets canvas'. Only the Google blog states this.

dropped.claim: Google's Terminal-Bench 4.1 comparison: Hydrogen scores 57% versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash.
dropped.evidence: Google: 'more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%)'. Only the Google blog states this.

dropped.claim: Hydrogen has a native 1 million-token input window and up to 1 million output tokens.
dropped.evidence: Google: 'native 1 million-token input with up to 1 million output tokens'. Notebookcheck and Digital Trends mention only the 1 million-token context window (Notebookcheck, in the pricing context), not the output limit.

dropped.claim: Google introduced Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which switches between models such as Carbon and Hydrogen in one session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it used on average 24% less quota and finished 19% faster.
dropped.evidence: Google: Orchestrator 'reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster'. Only the Google blog states this.

dropped.claim: Free Gemini app users mostly still get Flash-Lite; Google AI Plus ($4.99/month) now lists Hydrogen as its headline model, and Google AI Pro is $19.99 and includes Gemini 4 Argon.
dropped.evidence: Notebookcheck: 'Google AI Plus at $4.99 per month now lists Gemini 4 Hydrogen as its headline model'; 'Google AI Pro at $19.99, which also includes Gemini 4 Argon'; free users 'mostly still get Flash-Lite'. Notebookcheck notes Google's help page still lists Pro models under AI Plus, so Google's pages disagree. Single source.
